v.why: An identity shortcut on 0->3 makes the cell residual so the 2->3 branch only refines the signal, buffering the cost of shrinking it to 1x1.
When 2->3 is parameter-free, a 3x3 conv on the shortcut becomes a primary learned input to node 3 and adds more than when 2->3 is already a conv.
With a 3x3 conv already feeding node 3 from node 1, another 3x3 on 0->3 gives diminishing returns.
With 1->3 pruned, node 1 reaches the output only through 1->2->3, so a conv on edge 2 adds real depth instead of competing with a shallow bypass.
If 0->2 already applies a 3x3 conv, another 3x3 into node 2 duplicates capacity and yields a smaller gain.
A conv on 0->1 pays off only if node 1 is consumed downstream, and a conv on 1->2 both guarantees that and forms a deeper conv stack.
When node 1 is a conv output, a skip on 1->3 delivers a distinct processed feature to the output instead of a near-duplicate of the input.
With no direct 0->3 shortcut, a skip on 1->3 becomes the cell's nearest residual path and helps optimization substantially.
When 1->2 is pruned, node 2 holds only what edge 1 supplies, so pooling there turns the whole 2->3 branch into blurred raw input.
When 2->3 delivers only pooled features, a learned 3x3 on 1->3 becomes the main source of sharp discriminative features at node 3.
